build_spec:
# Morning Board — Build Specification

## Overview

Morning Board is the D-MB5/D-MB6 slice that turns the PA prototype's
hand-planted morning message into a registered gallery app. It does three
things every morning: (1) **stocks** the shared Board store from the bot's
already-connected sources (calendar on by default; email only when the
operator has granted it), (2) **composes** one numbered morning message
from the store, and (3) **delivers** it — as the daily chat message AND as
the board page's collapsible briefing panel, the SAME composition
delivered twice (D-BI6d).

Morning Board does NOT own the board store. The store lives on the admin
daemon (`{shared_dir}/boards/<bot_id>/board.json`) and is written ONLY by
the daemon (D-MB1) — this app's script is a **client**, not a second
writer. Every read/write of a card goes through the admin daemon's
bot-facing API, `/api/board-bot/...`, over its unix socket
(`{shared_dir}/admin-daemon.sock`); the kernel's peer-uid check on that
socket IS the auth, so the script sends no credential of its own — the
same trust model `packages/plugin/src/tools/BoardTool.ts` uses for chat
triage.

This app REPLACES the hand-planted `morning-board` OC cron the PoC bot ran
during WoZ-1 (`internal/design-pa-board-2026-08-31.md` §7) — install
migrates that prototype's state into the real store and retires its cron
(D-MB6; see "Install-time migration" below). Without this app, the
prototype's morning message was invisible to the delivery monitor for
~10 weeks (`internal/baseline-pa-bot-2026-08-31.md`, "zero registered
producers"); this app's `scheduled_actions[]` + `delivery_contract` fix
that by construction.

**Cost discipline (D-BI6a, `internal/finding-cost-forensics-power-bot-2026-09-04.md`):**
the whole run — stocking, composing, delivering — is a deterministic tool
path. It makes **exactly one bounded model call**, for the short greeting
line only, never an agentic loop. A loop over this same task was measured
at ~$2/turn in the forensics finding; this run's one Haiku call is
~$0.0002.

---

## File Layout

```
scripts/
  morning_board.py           ← main CLI: run | preview | status
  morning-board-cron.sh      ← cron trigger (calls morning_board.py run)
morning_board/
  config.json                ← per-bot configuration (created on first run)
memory/
  board-runs/
    YYYY-MM-DD.json          ← one file per day: composed message + counts + cost
```

All paths are relative to the bot's workspace root
(`/Users/{bot_id}/.openclaw/workspace/`). The script never writes to the
board store directly — only through the admin daemon's socket API — and
never reads or writes outside the workspace except (a) the bot's
`openclaw.json` (read-only, to discover the Anthropic API key), (b) the
pod's `network.json` (read-only, to resolve the delivery route and this
bot's id), (c) `{shared_dir}/admin-daemon.sock` (the board API transport),
and (d) the launchd plist at `/Library/LaunchDaemons/` (installed once at
deploy time).

---

## morning_board/config.json — per-bot configuration

Create on first run if absent:

```json
{
  "user_name": "{user_name}",
  "time_zone": "{time_zone}",
  "delivery_time": "{delivery_time}",
  "model": "claude-haiku-4-5",
  "sources": {
    "calendar": true,
    "email": false
  }
}
```

The operator edits this file freely. `sources.email` stays `false` until
the operator explicitly grants email stocking through the access model
(D-BI6b) — an email-derived card is untrusted input and can never
auto-execute an action, only ever surface as something to look at. An
empty string for `model` forces the template composer.

---

## Stocking (calendar on by default, email opt-in — D-BI6b)

Reads the SAME cache files the hand-planted prototype read — no new
integrations:

- **Calendar Sync (`p-fe9acef3`)** — `memory/calendar-today.json`:
  `{id, title, start_iso, end_iso, attendees, description, is_external,
  location}` per event. Enabled by default.
- **Email Integration (`p-341576fa`, optional)** — `memory/email-digest.json`.
  Only consulted when `sources.email` is `true`.

Each candidate is POSTed to the daemon's `/api/board-bot/cards` — the
daemon does the stocking dedup server-side (D-BI2: a card matching an
already-`done`/`dropped` card's `source_id` or normalised title+day is
skipped, never re-added). The script never re-implements that check; it
always posts and trusts the `skipped` field in the response.

```python
def stock_from_calendar(events: list) -> int:
    added = 0
    for ev in events:
        if not isinstance(ev, dict):
            continue
        title = str(ev.get("title") or "").strip()
        if not title:
            continue
        enrichment = {}
        if ev.get("start_iso"):
            enrichment["when"] = {"value": ev["start_iso"], "source": "calendar"}
        if ev.get("location"):
            enrichment["location"] = {"text": str(ev["location"]), "source": "calendar"}
        result = board_add(
            title=title, cluster=guess_cluster(title, "work"),
            source="calendar", source_id=str(ev.get("id") or ""),
            enrichment=enrichment or None,
        )
        if not result.get("skipped"):
            added += 1
    return added
```

Email-derived cards carry `source: "email"` and a note saying so; they are
never treated as actionable on their own (D-BI6b — the lethal-trifecta edge
means an email-derived card can prompt "draft a reply", never an auto-send).

---

## The board client (unix socket, no credential of its own)

```python
class _UnixSocketHTTPConnection(http.client.HTTPConnection):
    def __init__(self, socket_path, timeout=None):
        super().__init__("localhost", timeout=timeout)
        self._socket_path = socket_path

    def connect(self):
        sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
        sock.connect(self._socket_path)
        self.sock = sock


def _board_request(method, path, body=None, timeout=10.0):
    conn = _UnixSocketHTTPConnection(str(_ADMIN_SOCKET), timeout=timeout)
    payload = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"} if payload else {}
    conn.request(method, path, body=payload, headers=headers)
    resp = conn.getresponse()
    return resp.status, json.loads(resp.read() or b"null")
```

`_ADMIN_SOCKET = Path("/Users/Shared/evolve/admin-daemon.sock")` (Linux:
`/var/lib/evolve/admin-daemon.sock`). A connection failure (socket
missing, `ECONNREFUSED`) means the daemon is down — the run FAILS loudly
(`BOARD_FAILED:` to stderr, exit 1) rather than silently skipping: the
board is the one source of truth (D-MB1), so a run that cannot reach it
has nothing to stock or compose from.

`board_list_active()` calls `GET /api/board-bot/cards?limit=200` and keeps
only `inbox`/`today`/`later` lanes — `done`/`dropped` are settled and
belong to the weekly receipt, not the morning message.

---

## Composing the message (one bounded model call)

Cards are grouped by the canonical cluster order (health, fitness, travel,
work, social, hobbies, family, home, admin — any custom cluster sorts
after, alphabetically) and numbered **once, sequentially, across the whole
board** — not restarted per cluster, because the reply-triage names one
global number:

```python
def number_and_group(cards):
    by_cluster = {}
    for c in cards:
        by_cluster.setdefault(str(c.get("cluster") or "admin"), []).append(c)
    order = list(_CLUSTER_ORDER) + sorted(k for k in by_cluster if k not in _CLUSTER_ORDER)
    lines, n = [], 0
    for cluster in order:
        rows = by_cluster.get(cluster)
        if not rows:
            continue
        lines.append(cluster.capitalize())
        for card in rows:
            n += 1
            lines.append(f"{n}. {card.get('title')}")
        lines.append("")
    while lines and lines[-1] == "":
        lines.pop()
    return lines, n
```

Zero cards renders as **"Nothing waiting this morning."** — never an empty
list or a skipped send. A day with cards ends with the reply-triage
legend: `Reply with a number and today / bot / later — e.g. "2 bot" hands
it to me.`

The ONE model call composes only the greeting line above the numbered
board — system prompt:

```
You write ONE short, warm morning-greeting sentence introducing a
person's task board for the day. You will be given the person's first
name (may be empty), today's local date, and a one-line summary of what
is on the board. Return ONLY that one sentence — no markdown, no quotes,
no signature, no board contents (those are appended separately). Use the
name once if it is non-empty. Do not invent anything not in the summary.
```

Call pattern is the same `urllib`-only, no-SDK call the Morning Briefing
app uses (`internal/spec-gallery-delivery-convention-2026-06-11.md`'s
canonical helper covers delivery; this is the same style applied to a
single Messages API call): `POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`,
`model: claude-haiku-4-5`, `max_tokens: 120`. If the call raises, times
out, or returns a markdown-fenced response, the run falls straight
through to the deterministic template greeting (`"Good morning" [, name]
+ "."`) — never crashes, never blocks delivery.

**Cost recording (build item 4).** Because this is a raw API call outside
the turn/annotation cost pipeline (it is not an OpenClaw agent turn), the
run records its own usage: `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, and a
`cost_usd` estimate from a small embedded per-model rate table (USD per 1M
tokens): `claude-haiku-4-5: (1.00, 5.00)`, `claude-sonnet-5: (2.00,
10.00)`. This lands in the run file below — the weekly receipt (D-PA2′)
sums `memory/board-runs/*.json`'s `cost_usd` for "your morning board cost
$X this week" with no new plumbing.

---

## Delivery (D-BI6d: composed once, delivered twice)

1. `openclaw message send` — the standard convention
   (`spec-gallery-delivery-convention-2026-06-11.md`): resolve the route
   from the canonical shared `network.json`
   (`/Users/Shared/evolve/network.json`, `_NETWORK_JSON` — NOT a bot-home
   or workspace guess) `bots.<id>.primary_user.external_ids`, deliver via
   the CLI,
   `True` only on an accepted send. `False` (no route) skips gracefully
   with `DELIVERY_SKIPPED:` and writes no run file — never a silent no-op
   dressed as success.
2. Only after the chat send is accepted: `POST /api/board-bot/briefing
   {text}` with the EXACT same composed text, so the board page's
   collapsible panel (`GET /board/<bot_id>/briefing`) shows the identical
   composition. This is best-effort — a failure here logs a warning but
   never turns an accepted chat delivery into a failed run; the chat
   message is the load-bearing evidence the delivery monitor reads.

## Idempotency + the run file

One run per day, enforced by `memory/board-runs/{date}.json`'s existence —
`run --force` is required to re-send. The run file is written ONLY after
`openclaw message send` accepts the delivery:

```json
{
  "date": "2026-09-14",
  "sent_at": "2026-09-14T14:00:03Z",
  "cards_shown": 3,
  "cards_stocked": {"calendar": 2, "email": 0},
  "sources_available": {"calendar": true, "email": false},
  "sources_enabled": {"calendar": true, "email": false},
  "composer": "llm",
  "model": "claude-haiku-4-5",
  "input_tokens": 140,
  "output_tokens": 18,
  "cost_usd": 0.00023,
  "message": "Good morning.\n\nHealth\n1. Dentist checkup\n\nWork\n2. Client call\n3. Review PR from Sam\n\nReply with a number and today / bot / later — e.g. \"2 bot\" hands it to me.\n"
}
```

**Load-bearing contract, do not change:** the run file is the delivery
monitor's `evidence.delivered` for this app's `scheduled_actions[0]` —
written ONLY after an accepted `openclaw message send`, never before,
never on a skip or a failure.

---

## Reply triage (guardrail — no new code here)

`packages/plugin/src/tools/BoardTool.ts` (D-MB4, shipped in
`board-tool-chat-parity-and-enrichment`, PR #4191) already implements
`board.list` / `board.add` / `board.move` / `board.assign` /
`board.progress` as thin daemon calls. This app does not add a chat tool —
it only relies on the bot's existing guidance to route a numbered reply
correctly: a reply naming a card number and `today` or `later` is a
`board.move` to that lane; a reply naming a card number and `bot` is a
`board.assign {owner: "bot"}` (D-BI7 — there is no "bot" lane to move
into). State this mapping in the bot's own guidance/system-prompt
material (`AGENTS.md`/`SOUL.md` or the app's own `usage.how_to_use`,
already carried below) — never invent a second tool for it.

---

## Install-time migration (D-MB6)

Retiring the WoZ-1 hand-planted prototype is an **operator-run recipe**,
not a hidden hook — the same shape `board_store.py`'s `import-tasks`
command already used, extended with a `migrate` subcommand
(`packages/admin/evolve_admin/board_store.py`):

```
python3 -m evolve_admin.board_store migrate \
    --bot <bot_id> \
    --tasks-file /Users/<bot_id>/.openclaw/workspace/memory/tasks.md \
    --events-file /Users/<bot_id>/.openclaw/workspace/state/board-events.jsonl
```

This imports every open row of the hand-planted `tasks.md` into the real
store (idempotent by title — `import_tasks_into_board`, unchanged), then
folds the hand-planted `state/board-events.jsonl`'s settle decisions (if
that file exists) onto the imported cards (`import_legacy_board_events` —
best-effort JSONL, `{"title": ..., "lane": "done"|"dropped"}` or
`{"title": ..., "done": true}` / `{"title": ..., "dropped": true}` rows;
anything else is skipped, never raised; idempotent — re-running settles
nothing a second time), then disables the hand-planted cron
(`launchctl bootout system/<label>`, default label
`ai.evolve.<bot_id>.morning-board` — the SAME label this app's own
`scheduled_actions[0]` installs under, so migrate-then-install lays the
new managed plist down cleanly where the hand-planted one used to run).
Every step prints its own outcome line — "says so in the install log" is
this command's stdout, which the operator captures however they capture
install output. `--skip-cron-disable` leaves the hand-planted cron running
for a dry run; `--legacy-cron-label` overrides the default when the
prototype used a different label.

The board store OUTLIVES this app: uninstalling Morning Board does not
delete `{shared_dir}/boards/<bot_id>/`.

---

## Test sequence

1. `python3 scripts/morning_board.py status` with no run file yet →
   "No board sent today yet." (exit 0).
2. `python3 scripts/morning_board.py preview` against a fixture board (no
   admin daemon reachable) → `BOARD_PREVIEW_FAILED:` to stderr, exit 1
   (there is nothing to preview without the store).
3. Against a running daemon with a stocked, empty board → preview prints
   the day-one "Nothing waiting this morning." message, honestly.
4. `run` twice in the same day → the second call prints `BOARD_SKIPPED:`
   and does not re-send or rewrite the run file.
5. `run --force` → re-sends and overwrites today's run file.
6. Cluster grouping + numbering match the fixture board exactly, including
   custom-cluster ordering after the canonical nine.

LaunchDaemon plist path: `/Library/LaunchDaemons/ai.evolve.{bot_id}.morning-board.plist`.

scheduled_actions.summary: Daily morning board — edit install.schedule.cron to change the time. Stocks from Calendar Sync (and, if granted, Email Integration), composes one numbered message, delivers via the bot's channel AND the board page's briefing panel. heal:rerun is safe: the run file enforces one delivery per day, so a forced re-run after a successful send is a no-op.

trigger_recognition.pattern: Morning Board fires once daily at 7am. If the user asks for a preview off-cycle, use `preview`; if they want to know whether it ran, use `status`. A reply that names a card NUMBER and today/later is a board.move to that lane; a reply naming a number and 'bot' is a board.assign(owner=bot) — use the existing board tool, never a new one.

usage.how_to_use: Background launchd fires `run` at 7am. For an off-cycle preview without stocking or sending, use `preview`. Use `status` to confirm the scheduled run delivered. A numeric reply to the morning message is board triage: '<n> today' or '<n> later' moves that card; '<n> bot' hands it to the bot.
bot_voice_examples: Board already sent at 7:02am — 3 items, 1 in health, 2 in work.
Nothing waiting this morning — board's clear.
